title: Biosency BoraConnect — Medical web platform
descriptor: Doctor / patient platform for remote monitoring
summary: Medical telemonitoring web platform connecting doctors and patients, with real-time alerts and serverless architecture.

details.tagline: A medical platform that turns patient signals into clinical decisions.

need.context: Biosency, a MedTech specialised in home monitoring, needed a single platform to serve both doctors and patients.
need.problem: No tool was able to centralise patient alerts, scale with the user base, and meet healthcare data constraints.
need.objective: Build a reliable, secure and scalable platform with a dual doctor / patient focus.

stakes: Guarantee the reliability of medical alerts
Scale without infrastructure cost overruns
Meet healthcare data constraints

solution.what: An Angular web application backed by a serverless API Gateway + Lambda architecture on AWS.
solution.why: Serverless allows pay-per-use pricing and absorbs alert spikes without pre-provisioning infrastructure.
solution.how: Split into Lambda micro-functions, exposed securely through API Gateway and an Angular front-end built around the medical workflow.

features: Serverless API that scales on demand
results: Live platform used by healthcare professionals
Architecture able to absorb spikes without intervention
Infrastructure costs aligned with real usage

title: Biosency BoraConnect — Medical mobile platform
descriptor: Patient mobile app for iOS and Android
summary: Cross-platform mobile application for remotely monitored patients, sharing the same serverless API as the web platform.

details.tagline: A single codebase for iOS and Android, plugged into the medical API.

need.context: Biosency patients needed smooth mobile access for their day-to-day monitoring.
need.problem: Maintaining two separate native apps would have doubled development and maintenance costs.
need.objective: Deliver a native mobile experience on iOS and Android from a single codebase.

stakes: Offer a smooth and reassuring patient experience
Share code between web and mobile
Keep the same serverless API to reduce complexity

solution.what: An Angular application wrapped in Capacitor, shipped to the App Store and Google Play.
solution.why: Capacitor exposes native APIs while reusing the Angular ecosystem already in place on the web.
solution.how: Reuse of the web business layer, integration of native notifications and publication on both stores.

features: iOS and Android app from a single codebase
results: One team for two mobile platforms
Shorter production lead times
Patient experience consistent with the web

summary: Brit Hotel group corporate website built for the AtoutGraph agency, with a booking interface and pages for each hotel.

need.problem: An ageing corporate website with poor performance that did not match the strength of the network.
need.objective: Rebuild the corporate site to reflect the size and diversity of the group.

Handle the diversity of properties
Hold up under high-demand periods

solution.why: A stack mastered by the agency, robust and aligned with existing hosting constraints.
solution.how: Template design, multi-hotel content integration and connection to booking modules.

Stack maintainable by the agency over time
Traffic and brand image consolidated

summary: Institutional website of the City of Saint-Malo built for the AtoutGraph agency, with editorial content management and citizen services.

Make in-house content editing easy

Easier updates for internal teams
Clearer and more accessible citizen information

title: AtoutGraph — In-house agency CMS

summary: CMS built in-house at AtoutGraph to produce and maintain the agency's client websites, based on PHP and Laravel.

details.tagline: The engine the agency uses to ship every client website.

results: Several client websites delivered on the same base
Shorter production lead times
Full stack ownership for the team

title: Agency Scraper — Automated apartment search
descriptor: Personal Go scraper — alerts on every new listing
summary: Personal Go scraper that monitors 15 real estate agencies continuously and sends a mobile notification every time a new listing appears.

details.tagline: Be the first on a real estate listing, without refreshing 15 sites by hand.

need.context: On a tight real estate market, the best listings disappear within minutes.
need.problem: Manually monitoring 15 agency websites is impossible, and public feeds are too slow or non-existent.
need.objective: Automate monitoring to receive a mobile notification as soon as a new listing appears.

stakes: Spot a new listing before anyone else
Stay light on the scraped sites
Run 24/7 without intervention

solution.what: A Go scraper that polls 15 agencies every minute and sends a mobile notification on every new listing.
solution.why: Go's native concurrency and low memory footprint are ideal for a continuously running service.
solution.how: Concurrent polling loop, diff against a local index, push notification whenever a new listing ID appears.

results: Listing alerts received in under a minute
No manual supervision needed
Near-zero server footprint

title: CrzGames — Game studio website
descriptor: Main studio site with dashboard and store
summary: Full website for the CrzGames video game studio: showcase, store, admin dashboard and launcher orchestration.

details.tagline: The studio control point: showcase, store, dashboard and launcher in one place.

need.context: CrzGames, an independent game studio, needed a centralised platform to run its products.
need.problem: No single entry point: showcase, store, launcher orchestration and back-office were fragmented.

Keep full ownership of data and business logic

solution.why: Vue 3 + Adonis provide a clear, performant and maintainable TypeScript stack.
solution.how: Decoupled front / back architecture, dashboard to manage content and store, typed shared API.

Modern stack maintainable solo
Shared technical base across multiple products

Player accounts unified across the whole ecosystem
Capacity to absorb announcement spikes

title: CrzGames Launcher — Multi-platform software
descriptor: Desktop launcher for Windows / macOS / Linux
summary: Cross-platform Steam-like launcher, proprietary to the studio, to distribute and launch CrzGames games on Windows, macOS and Linux.

details.tagline: A Steam-like launcher, but proprietary to the studio.

need.context: CrzGames distributes its games directly, without relying on a third-party platform.
need.problem: No clean way to install, update and launch games across the three desktop systems.
need.objective: Build a cross-platform launcher for Windows / macOS / Linux, proprietary and lightweight.

stakes: Stay in control of game distribution
Offer a native experience on three OSes
Minimise software size and footprint

solution.what: A Tauri v2 launcher (Rust on the native side) with a Nuxt v4 + Tailwind front-end for the UI.
solution.why: Tauri produces very lightweight native binaries compared to Electron, with Rust for the system layer and a familiar web front.
solution.how: Nuxt front embedded in Tauri, communication through Rust commands, downloads and updates handled natively.

results: Autonomous distribution of studio games
Native experience on three OSes from a single codebase
Updates fully owned by the studio

title: SeaTyrants Wiki — Game documentation
summary: Wiki dedicated to the SeaTyrants MMORPG, built with VitePress for fast, static documentation that is easy to contribute to.

need.objective: Deliver a fast, readable, easy-to-contribute wiki without spinning up heavy infrastructure.

Allow simple contributions (Markdown)
Keep maximum load performance

solution.what: A VitePress static site, deployable in seconds and editable in Markdown.
solution.why: VitePress is built for documentation: static, fast, easy to maintain and ideal for a technical wiki.
solution.how: Game-specific navigation, Vue components for rich content, static deployment.

results: Wiki live for the game's community
Easy contributions from editors
Maximum load performance

title: SeaTyrants — Anti-bot AI
descriptor: Real-time bot detection via ONNX Runtime
summary: Embedded AI system to detect players using bots in the SeaTyrants MMORPG, based on ONNX models executed in C/C++.

details.tagline: An AI that exposes bots before they rot the game.

need.context: The SeaTyrants MMORPG is exposed to automated behaviours that degrade the experience of legitimate players.
need.problem: Classic heuristics fall short against increasingly sophisticated bots.
need.objective: Detect bot behaviours in real time from gameplay signals, without penalising honest players.

stakes: Protect the game's economy and fairness
Hold real-time performance on the server side
Limit false positives on legitimate players

solution.what: An ONNX Runtime integration in C/C++ that loads trained models and evaluates them on gameplay signals.
solution.why: ONNX Runtime allows ML inference directly on the server side, natively, with minimal latency.
solution.how: Offline training pipeline, ONNX export, C/C++ inference plugged into the server-side gameplay flows.

features: Models retrained and redeployed without touching the binary
results: Server-side bot detection without degrading the experience
Inference latency compatible with a real-time MMORPG
Ability to iterate on models independently from the game

title: SeaTyrants GameServer — MMORPG infrastructure
descriptor: High-frequency UDP game server on Kubernetes
summary: Full game server infrastructure for SeaTyrants: Kubernetes with one pod per map, UDP server (forked ENET), 128 Hz tick rate, Quilkin proxy and event-driven NATS bus.

details.tagline: An MMORPG infra that holds 128 Hz, map per map, behind a UDP proxy.

need.context: SeaTyrants is a real-time MMORPG that must serve thousands of players with low latency and a high server tick rate.
need.problem: No infra capable of splitting maps, holding 128 Hz per tick and routing UDP traffic in a scalable way.
need.objective: Build a Kubernetes infrastructure able to scale per map and hold real time on the UDP network.

stakes: Hold a 128-tick-per-second cadence on the server side
Scale horizontally map by map
Route UDP traffic reliably and efficiently
Manage concurrency (mutex, multi-threading) without breaking the tick rate

solution.what: A Kubernetes infrastructure where each game map maps to a dedicated pod, powered by a UDP server forked from ENET, an event-driven NATS bus and a Quilkin UDP proxy at the edge.
solution.why: Splitting per map allows independent scaling, Quilkin handles UDP routing, NATS decouples services, and ENET remains one of the most solid UDP protocols for real-time games.
solution.how: One pod per map, multi-threading and mutexes on the game process side, NATS for cross-service events, Quilkin for UDP routing, infra-side load balancers to absorb load.

features: One Kubernetes pod per game map
UDP server based on a fork of ENET
128 Hz tick rate on the server side
NATS event bus for inter-service communication
Quilkin UDP proxy and infra-side load balancers
results: Infra capable of holding real time for an MMORPG
Per-map scalability without breaking server tick rate
Event-driven architecture ready to evolve

title: CrzGames - RC2D (2D game engine)
descriptor: C-based 2D engine with SDL3 and cross-platform modules
summary: A native C99 2D engine built with SDL3, designed to keep full independence from third-party 3D engines.

details.tagline: A proprietary 2D engine to keep full control of the tech stack.

need.context: CrzGames needed a long-term technical foundation for its 2D games without relying on external engines.
need.problem: Third-party engines can impose licensing, roadmap and runtime constraints that are risky for an indie studio.
need.objective: Build a complete, portable and modular 2D engine in C, fully owned by the studio.

Maintain reproducible builds across platforms
Deliver native C performance

solution.what: RC2DCore implemented in C99 with CMake and GitHub Actions CI/CD.
solution.why: This foundation provides tight control over performance, memory behavior and dependency lifecycle.
solution.how: Modular architecture, locked dependencies, native desktop/mobile builds and versioned release pipelines.

features: Rendering, input and GPU via SDL3
Text, image and audio through SDL3_ttf, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer
Optional networking, data, video and ONNX AI modules
Criterion unit tests and multi-platform publishing
results: In-house 2D engine maintained by CrzGames
Unified build chain for desktop and mobile targets
Stable technical base for future games

title: CrzGames - RCNET (game server engine)
descriptor: C++ server engine for UDP, microservices and orchestration
summary: A C++17 server engine built around RCNETCore to run performant, distributed and reproducible game backends.

details.tagline: A modular server engine for modern multiplayer architectures.

need.context: CrzGames needed a robust server engine for multiplayer game services.
need.problem: Manually assembling networking, security, orchestration and inter-service communication creates high operational complexity.
need.objective: Deliver a single industrialized and versioned server foundation around RCNETCore.

stakes: Ensure reproducible builds on all supported OSes
Stabilize UDP, HTTP and service-to-service communication
Provide native Kubernetes/Agones integration

solution.what: RCNET in C++17 with CMake, pinned dependencies and automated CI/CD.
solution.why: A modular design allows fast evolution without breaking game server integrations.
solution.how: Dependency bootstrap from dependencies.txt, client/server examples, public include API and versioned docs.

features: UDP through RCENet and HTTP/HTTPS through cpp-httplib
Agones SDK + gRPC integration for Kubernetes orchestration
Release pipelines with automated versioning and changelog
results: Unified backend base for CrzGames projects
More reliable deployments on Windows, Linux and macOS
Lower long-term backend maintenance cost

title: CrzGames - RCENet (enhanced ENet fork for UDP)
descriptor: ENet fork focused on IPv6, encryption and network observability
summary: CrzGames-maintained ENet fork with full IPv6/IPv4 support, peer-level encryption, explicit timeout events and reliable packet ACK callbacks.

details.tagline: A hardened ENet fork for real-time multiplayer networking.

need.context: CrzGames networking requirements exceeded what standard ENet provided for production workloads.
need.problem: Core features were missing for IPv6 support, flexible encryption and precise disconnect/ACK event handling.
need.objective: Build a compatible but stronger ENet fork tailored to high-demand UDP game traffic.

stakes: Increase UDP transport security
Differentiate timeout disconnects from intentional disconnects
Track reliable packet acknowledgements more precisely

solution.what: RCENet implemented in C with multi-platform CI and native package distribution.
solution.why: Owning the fork makes it possible to ship critical networking features without waiting on upstream release cadence.
solution.how: Added ENetEncryptor, ENET_EVENT_TYPE_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT and reliable packet acknowledgement callbacks.

features: Acknowledgement callback on reliable fragmented packets
results: Safer and more observable UDP stack in production
Better incident handling for network failures
Reusable networking core for RCNET and CrzGames games
